questions.question: What does CLIP train its image and text encoders to do with a matched web image-caption pair?
options: Predict the caption's next word from the image with a language-model loss.
Place the image and caption embeddings near each other in a shared vector space.
Use separate embedding spaces that cannot compare image and text vectors.
Assign the image a supervised class label before encoding the caption.
questions.explanation: CLIP encodes both modalities into unit-normalized vectors in one shared space, then increases similarity for matched image-caption pairs relative to mismatches. Separate spaces would make the cross-modal cosine comparison used for retrieval undefined.

questions.question: In a batch of N paired examples, which entries are the positives in CLIP's symmetric InfoNCE loss?
options: Every pair in a row, because all captions describe the same image.
The diagonal image-caption pairs in both row-wise and column-wise cross-entropy.
The largest off-diagonal similarity in each row and column.
Only the diagonal entries in the image-to-text direction.
questions.explanation: For N matched pairs, image i’s positive caption is j=i, the diagonal of S; the symmetric loss applies cross-entropy to rows and columns. Using only image-to-text rows omits the reciprocal text-to-image matching task.

questions.question: What happens to the softmax distribution when CLIP's temperature tau is lowered while similarities stay fixed?
options: It becomes flatter, so every batch item contributes equally.
It changes the diagonal labels but leaves the logits unchanged.
It removes all negative pairs from the similarity matrix.
It becomes sharper, increasing pressure to separate hard negatives.
questions.explanation: The logits are similarity divided by τ. Lower τ magnifies their differences before softmax, concentrating probability on higher-similarity pairs and making hard negatives more consequential; raising τ would flatten the distribution.

questions.question: Why can SigLIP avoid the global embedding all-gather that softmax InfoNCE uses?
options: Each GPU computes a single softmax over every global image and text.
SigLIP drops all negative pairs and trains only on matched examples.
Each image-text pair has an independent sigmoid binary-classification loss.
SigLIP replaces image and text embeddings with class labels.
questions.explanation: SigLIP treats each matrix pair independently with a sigmoid binary label, so GPUs can compute local pair blocks without one global softmax over gathered embeddings. Dropping negatives would remove the comparisons that teach mismatches to score lower.

questions.question: A zero-shot classifier must choose among cat, dog, and bird using a frozen CLIP model. What decision rule does the lesson use?
options: Average image pixels by class and select the largest RGB channel.
Embed a text prompt for each class and choose the highest image-text cosine similarity.
Train a new classifier on labeled target images before comparing similarities.
Choose the class whose prompt has the fewest tokens.
questions.explanation: Zero-shot classification embeds a text template for each candidate class and the image, normalizes vectors, then chooses the class with highest cosine similarity. Training on labeled target images would add a learned classifier and no longer be zero-shot.

questions.question: One prompt template gives unstable zero-shot scores across classes. Which lesson-supported change can improve the text representation?
options: Use one longer prompt for the winning class after seeing its score.
Discard the text encoder and classify from image pixels alone.
Replace cosine similarity with a separate supervised softmax head.
Embed several templates per class and average their text embeddings.
questions.explanation: Averaging embeddings from several prompt templates makes each class representation less dependent on one phrasing; the lesson notes CLIP’s 80-template ensemble improved ImageNet accuracy. Apply the same template set to every candidate class, rather than using one longer prompt only for the class that already scored best.
